results.title: Gunmen hold two dozen people hostage at supermarket in Colombia's Cartagena
results.content: Armed robbers took roughly two dozen people hostage at a supermarket in Colombia’s tourist city of Cartagena on Tuesday, prompting a major police operation and a temporary suspension of incoming flights, authorities said. Landings at Rafael Nunez international airport resumed about 45 minutes later, after the military used a runway during the operation.

results.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Both sides are prepared to operate outside of the conflict zone'
results.content: Charli James is pleased to welcome Gavin Hall, Teaching Fellow in Political Science, and International Security at the University of Strathclyde. Hall examines recent Russian and Ukrainian operations beyond the main conflict zone, the conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement and the implications of diminishing direct US military support for Ukraine. “Both sides are prepared to operate beyond the main battleground and outside of the conflict zone,” he explains. Hall discusses why both sides want to negotiate from a position of strength and the conditions under which a “mutually hurting stalemate” could lead to a negotiated settlement.

results.title: Yemen’s army says Houthi fighters closing in on government stronghold of Aden
results.content: Yemen's military on Tuesday said that Houthi fighters were closing in on the internationally recognised government's stronghold of Aden from about 60km (40 miles) away and vowed to repel any assault. A military spokesman said defences were prepared following Houthi advances and government pullbacks near the Red Sea.

results.title: France's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy, wife Carla Bruni to stand trial for alleged witness tampering
results.content: France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering. The new charges are related to the Sarkozy couple's actions during the case examining illegal campaign funding from Libyan strongman Muammar Gaddafi over which Sarkozy was imprisoned last year.

results.title: 'We are ready to facilitate removal of Netanyahu': Head of Israel's Arab-majority Joint List
results.content: In an interview with FRANCE 24, the head of the Arab-majority Joint List said his political alliance is prepared to play a decisive role in bringing down Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government following the recent election. "We are ready to facilitate the removal of Netanyahu" from power, Yousef Jabareen said, signalling a willingness to explore political alliances beyond traditional divisions in Israeli politics.

results.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners
results.content: Senegal ​were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners ​on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title. Senegal contested the ​Confederation ‌of African Football's decision to declare ⁠Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in ‌January's final in Rabat. Morocco announced that it would “pursue all necessary legal procedures” in response to the decision.

results.title: 'Tis the season to be green: Can the Christmas holidays be a present for the planet?
results.content: With the holiday season just around the corner, we take a look at its environmental impact. We discuss how to make Christmas a little greener as consumers, whether plastic trees or natural ones are better for the planet, and what small steps we can all take to reduce our carbon footprint during the festivities.

results.title: French police officer who shot teenager to face murder trial
results.content: A French police officer will stand trial for murder in the killing of a teenager in 2023 that sparked violent protests across the country, the Versailles appeals court said on Tuesday. Nahel Merzouk, 17, was shot in the Paris suburb of Nanterre after he failed to comply with an order to stop his car.

results.title: Leaked data suggests 500,000 Russian soldiers killed since start of Ukraine invasion
results.content: More than 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war with Ukraine, according to an estimate by a number of media organisations. The figures are based on a huge dataset that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and a Ukrainian hacker group, Silent Crow. Two independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona say the death toll may rise to more than 700,000 once missing soldiers are included.

results.title: Burnham's EU reset brings back Brexit debate
results.content: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham accused predecessors who have warned him against reigniting the Brexit debate of being "stuck in the past", as he trumpeted his EU reset deal on Monday. Burnham has in recent weeks smashed a consensus that Britain's acrimonious departure from the European Union was done and dusted, floating the possibility that Britain could apply to rejoin. Clovis Casali takes a closer look.

results.title: 'Nina Roza' director: 'I was inspired by a real case of a child painter prodigy'
results.content: The director of a film nominated by Canada for next year's Oscars has told FRANCE 24 she was inspired by stories of a child painter prodigy, as well as the idea of identity and what you leave behind when you change countries. The film "Nina Roza" tells the story of a Bulgarian man who leaves his homeland with his daughter and sets himself up as an art curator in Canada.

results.title: UK’s Burnham on a mission to build public support EU reset
results.content: While he insists it would be unthinkable to rejoin the bloc without another referendum, British PM Andy Burnham has nevertheless reopened the debate over Brexit. After striking a deal that brings the UK and the EU closer on issues including food export control standards, youth mobility and carbon emissions, he's set to discuss the future of the relationship with Brussels in the coming weeks and will present the results of the talks in December. It comes despite criticism from a host of former Conservative prime ministers.

results.title: The French mayors refusing to back presidential candidates
results.content: Tuesday marks the opening in Paris of the 108th Congress of French Mayors, where the presidential race is a contentious issue. Candidates need 500 mayor endorsements to run, yet nearly half of mayors this year say they refuse to endorse anyone. France 2 and Caitlin Brown have more.

results.title: France's femicide orphans: The invisible victims of violence against women
results.content: In France, 111 women were killed by their current or ex-partners in 2025 alone, leaving behind dozens of children. How can they rebuild their lives without their mother? How can they seek help? In this episode of France in Focus, we meet Cloé and Eva-Louise, whose world collapsed when their father brutally murdered their mother. FRANCE 24's Natacha Vesnitch, Olivia Bizot, Clément Di Roma and Aurore Cloé Dupuis report.

results.title: 🔴Senegal regain AFCON title after successful appeal at sport arbitration court
Senegal regain AFCON title after successful appeal at sport arbitration court
results.content: The Court of Arbitration for Sport on Tuesday unanimously ruled in favour of Senegal in the appeal to reclaim the Africa Cup of Nations title, 10 months after a chaotic final against Morocco. Senegal won the match in January but was stripped of the title in March because many of the team's players had walked off the pitch in protest over a penalty given to the opposing side. Morocco said it would contest the ruling.

results.title: Rwanda's malaria cases on the rise: Climate change leads to more mosquitoes
results.content: In Rwanda, malaria cases are on the rise due to climate change. Higher temperatures and prolonged rainfall are creating more breeding grounds for mosquitoes. According to researchers, the risk of infection could increase by as much as 20 percent by 2100 in the Rift Valley. Our correspondent Aurore Bayoud reports on Rwanda's efforts to tackle the problem.

results.title: 'Political hunting ground': French presidential candidates campaign mayors' congress
results.content: Candidates in next year’s French presidential election descended on the 108th Congress of French Mayors in Paris on Tuesday, hoping to win endorsements for their campaigns. France 24’s Luke Shrago reports.

results.title: Trump's role in Huang's Nvidia return under scrutiny
results.content: Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia was greeted with triumph by US President Donald Trump, and the AI chipmaker's stock price was sent soaring. But the national security implications of Huang's extra-marital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, as well as Trump's intervention in the operations of a company in which he holds stock, have stirred anger in Congress, with members from both parties vowing to investigate.

results.title: In South Africa, parents' homemade sensory room helps children with ADHD
results.content: Determined to help their children, parents in a South African township have transformed a discarded shipping container into an underwater-themed sensory room using recycled plastic bottles, cut-out flowers and ferns. Originally designed for children with conditions including ADHD and epilepsy, the space is now benefiting the wider community.

results.title: DR Congo and Kenya agree to restore ties
results.content: After years of strained relations over the conflict in eastern Congo, Kinshasa and Nairobi are moving towards a diplomatic reset. DR Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi met his Kenyan counterpart William Ruto over the weekend and they agreed to to restore normal ties and deepen economic and regional cooperation. Emmet Livingstone reports.

results.title: Israeli strikes on Gaza kill senior Hamas security official and six other people, medics say
results.content: Israeli air strikes on the devastated Gaza Strip killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahel, director-general of the Palestinian territory's Internal Security Service on Tuesday, the ministry said. Another six people, including two police officers and a 17-year-old teenager, were killed in Israeli strikes across the enclave.

results.title: Advances in health and medicine: From space, ‘you discover things that are hidden' back on Earth
results.content: When kids look up at the night sky and marvel at the moon and the stars, the mysteries of space can spark a sense of wonder and curiosity. One of France's most beloved astronauts, Thomas Pesquet, joins Eve Irvine to take us one step beyond with his new book, "Space in 100 Questions", offering space enthusiasts of all ages an otherworldly glimpse into the Final Frontier!

results.title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO in sudden reversal after Trump intervention
results.content: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, drawing approval/plaudits/cheers from Wall Street and criticism from US lawmakers. The sudden reversal was the latest twist in the fallout from Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
